Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Insurance Group Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Insurance Group's Third Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Operating Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Claims Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Insurance Group's performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by continued improvements in our expense ratio through operational efficiencies and tech investments, favorable reserve development from disciplined actuarial practices, a robust capital position with growing statutory surplus, effective management of catastrophe losses within our risk appetite, solid realized gains offsetting unrealized investment pressures, pricing discipline boosting premium volumes, and strategic capital deployment into growth opportunities. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation initiatives, enhancing everything from claims processing to customer acquisition.

David, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

David Chen: Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $525 million, or $2.15 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included premium growth from rate adequacy, expense efficiencies, favorable reserve releases, managed catastrophe impacts, and resilient investment returns. Our combined ratio was 92.4%. Investment income for the quarter was $1.65 billion. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with statutory surplus at $19.2 billion. Our expense ratio also improved to 26.5%.

Let me dive deeper into some of these areas starting with expense ratio trends. I'm pleased to report continued progress on our operational efficiency front. Our consolidated expense ratio came in at 26.8% this quarter, down 170 basis points year-over-year from 28.5% and 40 basis points sequentially from Q2. This marks the sixth consecutive quarter of improvement, with our trailing 12-month expense ratio at 27.1%—well ahead of the industry average of 29.2% per AM Best for the P&C sector.

Breaking it down, policy acquisition costs were 12.4% of earned premiums, and general and administrative expenses were 14.4%. This efficiency underpins our combined ratio and positions us for mid-teens ROE expansion. Commissions, about 65% of PAC, rose modestly to 9.2% of premiums from 8.9% year-over-year, due to higher variable commissions linked to 14% premium growth in personal lines like auto and homeowners. In the agent channel, 58% of new business, street-level commissions averaged 7.5% on auto, amid competitive pressures and broker consolidation like at Travelers and The Hartford. But our direct-to-consumer digital channel offset this, with costs at 4.1% via programmatic advertising and the Apex Mobile app, now with 4.2 million monthly active users and 28% conversion on quotes.

Regionally, U.S. commissions were steady at 9.0%, supported by independent agency partnerships in the Southeast for cat-prone risks. In Europe, UK motor commissions hit 10.1% from FCA consumer duty enhancements and broker rebates, similar to Chubb. Asia-Pacific compressed to 7.8% through bancassurance with DBS in Singapore and ICBC in China.

On operating costs in G&A, we cut 6% year-over-year to $1.42 billion, or 14.4% of premiums, despite growth. Inflation on salaries and facilities added headwinds, but tech transformation countered: our AI-powered Apex Claims Engine processed 72% of auto claims under $10,000 straight-through, cutting adjuster time 41% and underwriting costs $28 million. Cloud migration to AWS saved $45 million run-rate on mainframes, RPA handled 1.2 million renewals dropping per-policy servicing to $17 from $24. Telematics penetration reached 35% in U.S. auto, aiding real-time pricing like Progressive's Snapshot.

U.S. ops costs improved 8% to 14.1% post our Acme Midwest acquisition. Europe was 15.2% with GDPR and flood claims, APAC 13.5% via Manila centers. Our Efficiency 2.0 roadmap targets sub-25% by 2026: doubling digital sales to 45%, gen AI for underwriting triage on 20% of commercial lines cutting cycles 15%, and ESG synergies for EU subsidies. We guide Q4 expense ratio at 26.5-27.0%, full-year 26.9%, fueling cyber parametric launches.

Next, reserve development trends have been a bright spot. In Q3, we recorded $275 million of net favorable reserve development across prior accident years, adding 85 basis points to our combined ratio. Year-to-date, $850 million favorable, up 15% from last year, or 2.8% of average carried reserves—high end of our 2-3% target. Primarily from 2021-2023 accident years, with losses 4-6% below initial triangles.

Personal lines, 55% of $18.2 billion net premiums written, drove $180 million favorable: $120 million in auto physical damage, where severity was $4,200 per claim, 5% below estimates as supply chains stabilized using CCC data. Homeowners added $40 million from subrogation in mild 2023 California wildfires.

Commercial lines: $75 million net favorable, $50 million from specialty casualty like E&S, where social inflation tracked 7% CAGR vs. assumed 10%, aided by ADR. Offset by $25 million unfavorable in workers' comp for 2021-2022 medical tails per NCCI.

U.S. (70% premiums): $210 million favorable post Guidewire rollout. Europe: $45 million in UK motor via IFRS 17. Continental property had $10 million unfavorable from German floods, capped by Swiss Re quota-share. APAC: $20 million net, Australia CTP offsetting Japan quakes.

Powered by AI IBNR modeling with telematics from 40% auto policies, reducing volatility 25%; stochastic simulations via MG-ALFA for tail risks; LAE at 8.2%. Conservative 75th percentile philosophy yields 2.5% five-year average vs. industry 1.8%. Full-year guide $900 million to $1.1 billion favorable, with reinsurance tower protecting.

Turning to catastrophe losses: $1.47 billion this quarter, 9.8% of GWP, nine months $2.85 billion or 7.9% of $36.2 billion GWP—up from 5.4% last year. Net incurred over $20 million threshold, post reinsurance.

U.S. (62% GWP): $920 million or 14.2%, from Rex Fire wildfires $450 million in property, Midwest/Southeast storms $320 million. Up 51% from Q3 2022, per Verisk/RMS.

Europe: $280 million or 7.1% from Storm Betty floods. APAC: $190 million Typhoon Doksuri/monsoons. LatAm resilient $80 million post non-renewals.

Trends: nine-month 7.9% in 7-9% corridor, frequency up 18%, secondary perils 45%. Severity moderated by codes/mitigation.

De-risked with $2.5 billion XL tower cheaper 15%, $300 million cat bond Summit Peak transferring NE hurricane risk, reducing retention 12%. RMS v23.0 trimmed CA exposure 5%. Parametric now 15% U.S. commercial, cutting lags 60%. Rates: U.S. +11.2%, CA HO-3 +22%. Full-year $3.9-4.3 billion or 8.2-9.0% of $47 billion GWP.

On investments: $152 billion assets. Conservative ALM: 72% fixed maturities (IG corporates/munis), 15% equities, 8% alts, duration 5.8 years.

Realized gains $187 million, up 42% YoY from trimming $2.1 billion low-yield bonds, BBB energy like Exxon, equities on tech rally. Redeployed to 4.85% new yield, book 4.3%.

Unrealized losses $412 million, AOCI deficit $2.8 billion: NA $285 million MBS on Treasury rise, Europe $78 million Bunds/OATs/UK gilts, offset by EM gains $18 million Mexico/Brazil.

ALM via Aladdin stress-tests, private credit up to $4.2 billion 7-9% yields, CAT bonds/ILS $350 million. Income up 11% to $1.62 billion, ROIP 4.3% topping peers. Q4 gains expected as duration to 5.5 years.

Pricing changes drove premium volume: GWP +9.2% to $14.8 billion, 11th double-digit quarter. Pricing 6.8 points, rates 7.2%; volume 1.5 points, retention 91.2%; mix 1.0 point to 62% commercial.

Commercial multi-peril: 12.4% rates, 11.8% growth. WC 9.1% rates, 8.7% growth. Homeowners 5.3% rates, 7.1% growth via UBI ZenithDrive Home 28% penetration. Auto +0.8% with 6.2% rates.

Regions: NA 8.1% rates, Europe 6.4%, APAC 14.2% growth 9.8% rates. AI engines with RMS/AIR, 150+ factors; telematics 4.2 million policies. Full-year Q4 rates 7.0-7.5%, GWP 8-10%.

Capital position: Statutory surplus $19.2 billion, up 12% YoY, top quartile S&P. RBC 285% consolidated, P&C 312%, L&A 245%.

Drivers: $1.4 billion operating earnings from 92.5% CR, 8.2% commercial/6.5% auto rates; $450 million reserves; 4.8% yield on $45 billion portfolio via corporates/munis.

Management: $750 million notes 4.75%, debt 22%; $900 million retained offset $500 million returns ($300 million buybacks, div $0.85 up 10%); $200 million sidecar.

Regions: U.S. $12.1 billion +14% post cats; Europe €3.2 billion SCR 195%; APAC $2.8 billion +18%. $1.5 billion M&A pipeline, ORSA stress-tests, $150 million cat modeling.

Year-end $20 billion target.

Capital deployment: $4.2 billion deployable, RBC 620%, leverage 22%. Framework: 40% organic/innovation, 30% tuck-ins, 20% returns, 10% reinsurance/tech. Hurdle 11%, ROE 14-16%.

Acquisitions: Closed $850 million incl. $550 million Midwest Heritage 1.1x book, 150 bps CR improve, cyber cross-sell. Pipeline $1.2 billion: Nordics cyber insurtech $400 million, SE Asia parametric $300 million, U.S. E&S MGUs—EPS accretive, specialties to 30% book.

New products: $1.1 billion R&D. Summit DriveSafe 2.0 telematics with Verizon, 22% LR cut, $750 million premiums. Embed API Shopify/Salesforce 12% conversion 88% CR, EV parametric. Europe longevity annuities, APAC flood parametric.

Tech: $450 million AWS/Snowflake/Palantir, 250 bps expense cut, blockchain claims. 8-10% EPS CAGR.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, David. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our personal auto line. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-driven pricing engines and telematics integration for real-time adjustments.

Robert Kline: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income and alternatives, with tactical realizations supporting higher yields.

Tom Hargrove: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including the Apex Claims Engine automating 72% of low-value auto claims. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times by 41% and enhanced subrogation recoveries.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the reserve development trends this quarter?

Michael Reynolds: Good morning, Emily. Absolutely. As David detailed, the $275 million favorable in Q3 and $850 million year-to-date reflect our conservative reserving at the 75th percentile, with personal auto and homeowners leading due to better severity outcomes than initially projected post-supply disruptions and mild weather. Our AI IBNR models and stochastic simulations continue to sharpen accuracy, positioning us for ongoing releases absent major shocks.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Thompson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mark Thompson: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of higher interest rates on your investment portfolio?

David Chen: Good morning, Mark. The rate environment drove $412 million in unrealized losses this quarter, mainly on fixed maturities amid Treasury and Bund yield rises, widening our AOCI deficit. However, realized gains of $187 million from opportunistic trims allowed redeployment into 4.85% new money yields, lifting book yield to 4.3% and ROIP to top peers. With expected Fed cuts, we anticipate easing pressure and modest Q4 gains as we shorten duration further.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Rachel Lee: What is the expected impact of emerging climate regulations on your underwriting strategy?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Rachel. Climate regs like EU Green Deal expansions are prompting us to integrate ESG risk scores into our GLMs, alongside RMS climate analytics. We've trimmed high-exposure areas like California homeowners by 5% and accelerated parametrics to 15% of commercial property, which pay on indices and reduce tail volatility. This, combined with rate hikes like 22% in CA HO-3, keeps our cat load at 6.5-9% of GWP while pursuing growth in resilient lines.

Operator: Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thanks. On capital deployment, any updates on M&A pipeline?

David Chen: Hi Alex. Our $1.2 billion authorization targets accretive bolt-ons like the Nordics cyber platform and SE Asia parametric reinsurer, building on Midwest Heritage synergies. These enhance specialties to 30% of book, with ROIC 12-14%, while new products like DriveSafe telematics project $750 million premiums at sub-65% LR.

Operator: Our final question comes from Sophia Grant with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Sophia Grant: Good morning. How are pricing changes influencing retention and new business?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Sophia. Earned rates of 7.2% drove 9.2% GWP growth, with retention at a five-year high 91.2% via mid-term tools capturing 65% indicated rate. New business up 12.1%, selective in E&S at 15-20% rates. Telematics and AI segmentation boost elasticity, ensuring profitability over volume.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
